newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Slot delays hit Cathay HK-Tokyo cargos.
newsitem.headline: Slot delays hit Cathay HK-Tokyo cargos.

text.p: Slot restrictions at Tokyo's Narita and Hong Kong's Kai Tak airports are delaying plans by Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd to start an additional freighter service between the two cities, James Barrington, general manager for Cathay Pacific Cargo told Reuters.
Cathay currently flies six Boeing 747 freighters a week to Tokyo and wants to add a seventh frequency to Narita either on Wednesdays or Fridays.

"We have government approval and want to start as soon as we can get slots into Narita combined with the slot situation at Kai Tak. It is just a case of getting slots at both ends," Barrington said in an interview.
He described Japan as Cathay's most profitable market for both passengers and cargo but because of airport constraints he does not see much opportunity for growth this year.
The demand to increase services was driven by the Hong Kong outbound market because the Japanese export market is "a bit weak." in comparison, he added.

Cathay increased its freight capacity between Hong Kong and Osaka earlier this month with the start of four new afternoon flights using Airbus A330-300 aircraft which makes it the largest carrier on the route,the airline said.
